speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start at the beginning: can you describe exactly how you noticed your gait and limb ataxia, and when these symptoms first started? Also, what specific medical conditions have you been diagnosed with in your significant medical history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, particularly on the right side, or any changes in your vision or balance when lying down? Also, do you have a history of diabetes, hypertension, or any previous strokes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to natalizumab therapy.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI with contrast.
REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR from cerebrospinal fluid.

You mentioned being on natalizumab for Crohn's; this medication carries a known risk of PML, which explains your sudden onset of ataxia and right-sided weakness. The brain scan and CSF test are critical to confirm this immediately.
